pressReleaseTitle: India Ratings Affirms B.G. Shirke Construction Technology at ‘IND A’/Stable; Rates Additional Term Loan
issuerName: B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd.
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has affirmed B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd’s (BGSCTPL) Long-Term Issuer Rating at ‘IND A’. The Outlook is Stable. The instrument-wise rating actions are as follows:
overviewHTML: Ind-Ra continues to consider BGSCPTL’s standalone financials to arrive at the ratings and has not consolidated the amount of guarantee extended to its related parties such as B G Shirke Redevelopment and Gas Pvt. Ltd. (BGSRGPL), Parijat Hill View Realty LLP (PHVR) and Teenmurthy Summit Realty LLP. (TSRLLP). However, Ind-Ra has factored in the debt guaranteed of these entities and the likelihood of any incremental support required by these entities to arrive at the ratings.
keyRatingDrivers:
Revenue Visibility Continues to be Strong:  BGSCPTL maintained a healthy unexecuted order book of INR150.14 billion at end-May 2021 (end-December 2020: INR159.6 billion), providing a revenue visibility of 5.1x of FY21 revenue (4.1x), and continued to supported by its strong execution capabilities. Construction work had ceased for a major portion of 1QFY21 due to the COVID-19-related lockdown, and the pace of construction remained slower-than-normal until November 2020. Consequently, the revenue fell to INR31.53 billion in FY21 (FY20: INR38.79 billion), though it was higher than the management’s estimates of INR28 billion. The figures for FY21 are provisional in nature. Despite the impact of the second wave of COVID-19 and associated disruptions, the company completed work to the tune of INR5.57 billon during April-May 2021. The company expects the pace of order execution to pick up from 2QFY22 and expects to report revenue of INR35 billion in FY22. 

 

Credit Metrics Remain Comfortable: Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s net leverage to fall below 1x from FY22, led by reduced debt levels. BGSCTPL's on-balance sheet debt remained stable at INR11.32 billion in FY21 (FY20: INR10.97 billion). However, the credit metrics weakened in FY21 due to the decline in absolute EBITDA. The net leverage (net on-balance sheet debt/operating EBITDAR) rose to 2.14x in FY21 (FY20: 1.41x) and the gross interest coverage (operating EBITDAR/gross interest expense) fell to 3.63x (FY20: 4.10x).

 

In FY21, BGSCTPL extended a corporate guarantee of INR0.301 billion to Parijat Hill View Realty LLP/ PHVRLLP (FY20: INR0.319 billion) and B. G. Shirke Oil & Gas India Private Limited Nil (INR0.170 billion), and a letter of undertaking of INR0.100 billion to Teenmurthy Summit Realty LLP/ TSRLLP (INR0.534 billion). The gross debt (adjusted for corporate guarantee and undertaking) remained stable at INR11.73 billion in FY21 (FY20: INR12 billion), and the net adjusted leverage (adjusted net debt/operating EBITDAR) stood at 1.03x (1.09x). 

 

Liquidity Indicator - Adequate: BGSCTPL had unencumbered cash and cash equivalents of INR4.2 billion in FY21 (FY20: INR3.5 billion and FY19: INR2.2 billion). Moreover, over the 12 months ended May 2021, the maximum and average utilisation of its fund-based working capital limits stood at 26% and 18%, respectively, and the average utilisation of the non-fund-based limits was 77%. The company’s fund-based and non-fund-based limits are largely from public sector banks, with limited presence of private banks.

 

The on-balance sheet debt of INR11.31 billion at FYE21 comprised terms loan amounting to INR6.50 billion, intercorporate deposits worth INR0.81 billion, working capital loans of INR3.36 billion and deposits from related parties of INR0.64 billion. The company has scheduled repayments of INR3.71 billion and INR1.42 billion in FY22 and FY23, respectively.

 

Healthy Free Cash Flow: Ind-Ra expects BGSCTPL’s cash flow from operations to decline in FY22, given the reduced profitability and increased working capital needs. BGSCPTL’s cash flow from operations declined to INR1.99 billion in FY21 (FY20: INR4.1 billion) due to lower EBITDA levels coupled with an increase in raw material and other inventory. However, despite an increase in the inventory days (including unbilled revenue) to 227 days in FY21 (FY20: 192 days), the overall net working capital days improved to 18 days (25 days), led by a rise in the payable days (including mobilisation advances) to 209 days (167 days). The mobilisation advances from Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) and City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) do not entail an interest pay-out, while those from Delhi Development Authority (DDA) carry an interest. Furthermore, the capex declined to INR1.6 billion in FY21 (FY20: INR2.0 billion). Consequently, though the free cash flow fell, it continued to be positive at INR0.42 billion in FY21 (FY20: INR1.99 billion). The company is likely to incur capex of INR1.5 billion-2 billion each year over the near term.

 

Moderation in Margins: BGSCTPL’s absolute EBITDA moderated to INR5.29 billion in FY21 (FY20: INR7.79 billion), in line with Ind-Ra’s expectations, due to an increase in material costs (FY21: 60% of revenue; FY20: 56%), employee costs (9%; 8%) and direct expenses (14%; 12%). Consequently, EBITDA margins fell to 16.8% (20.1%), though the management had expected it to fall to 15% due to lower absorption of fixed costs. The management expects the company to record margins of 16%-17% over FY22-FY23.

 

Moderate Exposure to Group Entities: BGSCTPL’s loans and advances remained stable at INR3.47 billion in FY21 (FY20: 3.53 billion). Shirke Recreation Enterprise, Shirke Club Management LLP, TSRLLP, PHVRLLP and B G Shirke Redevelopment & Gas Pvt. Ltd jointly accounted for 94% of the total loans and advances in FY21 (FY20: 97%). BGSCTPL has extended corporate guarantees and letters of undertaking to group entities; however, the corporate guarantees extended to the group companies decreased to INR0.40 billion in FY21 (FY20: INR1.02 billion).

 

Slowdown in Order Inflow and Execution: The order inflows slowed down considerably in FY21 to INR10 billion (FY20: INR71 billion) on account of a decline in the number of orders placed by the end-customers due to procedural delays. Ind-Ra expects the order inflows to pick up in FY22. However, continued low order inflows will result in order book depletion and impact the revenue visibility over the long term. Additionally, in the scenario of low order availability, any bid by BGSCPTL with lower margins could exert pressure on its profitability.

 

Customer and Regional Concentration Remains High: BGSCTPL’s customer concentration remained high at end-May 2021 and the segmental diversification remained limited. CIDCO, DDA and MHADA, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana and Pimpri Chinchwad New Town Development Authority accounted for 37%, 21%, 15%, 11% and 5%, respectively, of the order book (end-December 2020: 40%, 22%, 15%, 10% and Nil, respectively). The concentration of the top 10 projects in the order book at end-May 2021 remained stable at 71% (end-December 2020: 71%). The orders from Mumbai Metropolitan Region account for 60% of the order book, followed by those from Delhi (21%), Pune, Nagpur and Nashik (10%), Southern India (7%) and others 2%. BGSCTPL continues to have a presence in only the prefabricated housing industry, in line with the management’s strategy to focus on its core strength wherein the company has a track record of over 30 years. At end-May 2021, work was yet to commence account for about 4.8% of the total orders. However, as confirmed by the management, the company has received approvals for the commencement of construction of a majority of projects in its order book. More than 75% of the order book is likely to be executed over FY22-FY23.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: An improvement in the free cash flow (cash flow from operations – interest expenses – capex), resulting in an improvement in the credit metrics, on a sustained basis, and/or a further decline in the support provided to group entities will be positive for the ratings. 

Negative: BGSCTPL’s gross coverage (EBITDAR/ interest cost) falling below 3.0x, on a sustained basis, could lead to a negative rating action.
companyProfile:
Incorporated in 1994 (established business in 1944), BGSCTPL is the flagship company of the Pune-based Shirke Group. BGSCTPL is primarily engaged in the construction of housing projects for government agencies such as DDA, MHADA, CIDCO and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is India's SEBI registered credit rating agency committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely, and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market.

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance companies, urban local bodies, and structured finance and project finance companies.

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India.

Ind-Ra is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.
